newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted little changed from their previous levels in thin trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
The market opened short of Z$139.8 million but the dealers said some treasury bill maturities had since injected liquidity into the system.

"The market is fairly quiet at the moment and rates seem to have sort of stabilised," one dealer said, alluding to the past month which saw the rates surge some six percentage points on the back of inflationary pressure.

On Wednesday the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$55 million worth of 62-day treasury bills at a yield of 22.96 percent, a notch up from 22.94 percent at Tuesday's sale. Call money was unchanged at 20 percent.
NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted at 24 percent (buying) from 25 percent while their selling rate edged up to 23.5 percent from 20 percent the previous day.
Bankers acceptances were being bought and sold at 23.5 and 22.5 percent respectively from Tuesday's 24 and 20 percent.
